chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Muawiya, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the free woman who performs Hajj to Mecca without a guardian, so he said: 'There is no problem with her going out with a reliable group.'

key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ الْحُرَّةِ: The free woman (as opposed to a slave or one under specific restriction)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Can a free woman perform Hajj without a male guardian?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of a free woman's Hajj journey, establishing that while a wali is generally preferred, her travel is valid if accompanied by a group of trustworthy men (qawm thiqat) rather than a single guardian. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the reliability of the companions ensuring her safety and religious integrity during the pilgrimage. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the flexibility in marital and travel restrictions within Shia jurisprudence.
